issues.title: Exact Dirac learning in a density-likelihood interface

failure_location.quote:
Therefore, our probabilistic model $q_{\theta}(u|a)$ learns a class of 
Dirac distributions $\delta_u(\cdot|a)$;

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the old probabilistic model exactly learns conditional Dirac distributions for noise-free outputs. The old paper actually supplies a pointwise density likelihood and a Gaussian reverse-process construction, whose noise-free final transition is degenerate; it supplies no well-defined density or log likelihood for the resulting Dirac endpoint. Since a Lebesgue density supported on a singleton integrates to zero rather than one, these ingredients support only a measure-valued or limiting approximation, not exact learning through the stated density interface.
issues.overall_effect: The exact noise-free density-likelihood interpretation and the associated exact-Dirac learning assertion are unsupported. This does not defeat the nonsingular noisy-data regime or numerical approximation of deterministic solutions.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the density-likelihood formulation to conditional laws having Lebesgue densities. For noise-free data, state that the target is a Dirac measure but that the density-based PDNO is trained on a positive-variance or positive-time smoothing and therefore only approximates the deterministic target, without assigning it an exact endpoint density or log likelihood.
issues.why_classification: Exact learning in the natural, advertised noise-free regime is a coherent substantive promise, so replacing it with a smoothed approximation is a limited weakening rather than a typo or routine qualification. The comparable noise-free approximation claim and all nonsingular noisy-data claims survive through a contained reformulation, so neither global reconstruction nor major mathematical loss is required.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: Therefore, in practice, we can run DDPM only on the interval $[t_{\text{start}}, T]$ and learn a generative model for sampling $U(t_{\text{start}}; a)$ instead.

issues.title: Conditional VLB mixes pointwise and population likelihoods
issues.failure_explanation: The old derivation equates $\log q_\theta(u_0\mid a)$, a function of the sampled u_0, with its scalar expectation under $p(u_0\mid a)$. In the allowed nondegenerate Gaussian-noise regime this equality requires the log density to be almost surely constant, which is not assumed. Jensen therefore yields a bound on the expected negative log likelihood, not the asserted pointwise quantity, and $L_0$ must be averaged over the joint law $p(u_0,u_1\mid a)$ rather than only $p(u_1\mid a)$.
issues.overall_effect: The conditional variational-bound derivation and its L_0 decomposition are invalid as written for noisy data. The final sample-averaged denoising loss can be retained after carrying the missing data-law expectation consistently.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the VLB for the population quantity E_{p(u0|a)}[-log qθ(u0|a)], define L0 using the joint law p(u0,u1|a), and carry that data-law expectation consistently through the decomposition and the final averaging over a. The resulting sample-averaged denoising objective may remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The pointwise-to-population equality is a genuine false inference and therefore not a typo. Correcting and propagating the missing expectation is nevertheless short, routine, and source-supported; it requires no new lemma and preserves the noisy-data model, the population VLB, and the final training loss without meaningful loss.

issues.title: Reverse covariance prescribed beyond the unit-Gaussian regime

diagnostic_evidence.quote: obtained from corrupting the output $u$ by an additive Gaussian noise $\eta \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \Sigma(a))$, i.e., $u_{\eta} = u + \eta$.

issues.failure_explanation: For each fixed input a, the old covariance prescription claims beta_t I for observations with additive Gaussian noise even though the admitted noise law is N(0,Sigma(a)). Taking Sigma(a)=cI with c not equal to 1 and one forward step gives $\operatorname{Var}(U_0\mid U_1)=c\beta/((1-\beta)c+\beta)\,\mathbf I$, not $\beta\mathbf I$. The old identity-covariance proposition therefore supports only the unit-covariance case, not the displayed general Gaussian branch.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed exact or optimal reverse covariance is unjustified for nonunit, anisotropic, or input-dependent Gaussian noise. The remaining DDPM construction is not thereby disproved, but this covariance branch needs restriction or a covariance depending on the actual data law.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict every exact, optimal, or full-path-likelihood claim for the β_t I reverse-covariance branch to the case U0|a distributed as N(m(a),I). For general nonunit Gaussian covariance, retain β_t I only as an explicitly approximate fixed reverse variance and state that no exact covariance guarantee is being made, while leaving the general noisy-data sampler otherwise available.
issues.why_classification: Nonunit, anisotropic, and input-dependent Gaussian noise forms a natural and explicitly admitted regime, so withdrawing the exact or optimal covariance guarantee there is substantive and exceeds a minor technical-premise correction. The loss is limited, however: the executable general sampler and the exact unit-Gaussian subcase remain through a contained qualification, with no need for global proof reconstruction.

issues.title: Dirac-entropy proposition includes an undefined t=1 endpoint

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We denote $H_p(X)=-\int_\mathcal{X} p_X(x)\log p_X(x)\,dx$ the entropy of $X\sim p_X(x)$.
where $p_{(X, Y)}$ is the joint density of $(X, Y)$ and $p_{Y|X=x}$ is the density of $Y$ conditioned on $X = x$.

issues.failure_explanation: Under the old density-based definition, the terms $H_p(u_0\mid u_1)$ and $H_p(u_0\mid u_0)$ occurring when t=1 are undefined because their conditional laws are Dirac. Thus the proposition's stated range t=1 through T invokes entropy outside the definition available in the paper.
issues.overall_effect: The proposition is not meaningful at its first time step under the old definitions. Its nonsingular t at least 2 content is unaffected, and the endpoint can be repaired locally.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Under the existing density-based entropy definition, change the proposition’s range to t=2 through T and identify t=1 as a singular endpoint outside that definition. The nonsingular statement and proof require no other change.
issues.why_classification: The defect is confined to one exceptional degenerate endpoint, has no listed downstream propagation, and is removed by a short routine domain correction that preserves all nonsingular content. It is not a typo because the old definitions do not uniquely force this repair rather than an added singular-entropy convention, and the proof presently invokes undefined quantities.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: By convention, we define the entropy of a Dirac distribution to be $-\infty$.
